Advances a connected electrochemical experiment by one simulation step.
The circuit clock calls this once per circuit and step; a live

members.name: activeInstruments
members.description: The instruments that are switched on right now, one marker each.

members.name: circuitIdentity
members.description:
The physical circuit a device belongs to, as a value that changes when
the wiring does: the members it reaches and the vessel each of them
dips into. A moved electrode, a new lead or a placed bridge re-keys the
circuit, and its clock starts a fresh phase.

members.name: advanceCircuit

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: an active instrument of the circuit

members.description:
One simulation step of a circuit, driven by its clock instead of by
every instrument that hangs in it. A live transient books its own
analytic readings, so the chemistry waits for it.

members.name: reconcileCircuits
members.description:
Brings the circuit clocks in line with the instruments that are
switched on. Called whenever a lead, a bridge, a device or an
instrument changes, so a clock never outlives the circuit it belongs
to.

members.name: meterCircuit
members.description:
The devices of a network that carries no cell: a supply wired straight
into a meter.

chemlib.Simulation.sEChem needs two electrodes, so a circuit
without them is read by chemlib.Simulation.sCircuit instead. A
network that carries an electrode is left to the cell solve, and one
without a supply has nothing to measure.

members.name: bridgeBetween
members.description:
The salt bridge on the canvas that joins the two half-cells of a
circuit, if there is one. The bridge carries no cable, so its two legs
decide: it has to dip into both vessels for the ionic current to close
the cell. The bridge itself is returned because its length and bore
decide how well it conducts.

members.name: cellCurrent
members.description:
The current the cell between the two electrodes carries, in ampere.
A supply that also feeds a lead laid across the electrodes delivers
more than the cell takes, and the law of Faraday is about what happens
at the electrodes, not about what leaves the supply.

members.name: clearEChemReadings
members.description:
Clears the readings a stopped experiment left behind. The cell solve
writes the voltage and the current of every device in the circuit, not
only of the one that was switched on, so the meters would otherwise keep
showing the last value they saw.

The footprint is measured on a throwaway preview, because the real view

members.description:
Joins two devices with a cable. This is the single entry point for
wiring: the canvas drag, the restore path and the settings panel all go
through it, so a cable always lands in the same three places - the
device terminals, the component list and the canvas.

members.name: authorCable

parameters.name: sprite
parameters.description: its view, which the entry is found by

members.description:
Records a cable that was laid by dragging in the data block. The partner
lists of the two devices cannot carry it: they name each partner once,
so a second lead between the same pair would be lost. The cable entry
names the device on each of its ends instead, which keeps parallel leads
apart and brings them back one by one.

members.name: syncAuthoredConnections
members.description:
Rewrites the authored connection list of a device from its live
terminals. The order is what matters: `polarity` names the electrode on
terminal 0, so a rewire has to be written back in terminal order rather
than appended.

A cable is written back as the device on each of its ends, with `null`
for an end that hangs free, so the position in the list is the end.

members.description:
Stores a reviewed structure as a palette reagent, a weighed solid or a
plain reference.

The weighed form exists only for a compound the catalog does not already
hold: a catalog solid is selected as that reagent instead, so the palette
never carries a second entry for one substance. Both forms keep the same
key, and both derive their recipe again from the current structure at the
moment of use, so an edited structure cannot dose an old recipe.

members.name: scopedElements
members.default: { "chemlab-atomic-figure": AtomicFigure, "sl-badge": SlBadge, "sl-button": SlButton, "sl-card": SlCard, "sl-carousel": SlCarousel, "sl-carousel-item": SlCarouselItem, "sl-dialog": SlDialog, "sl-divider": SlDivider, "sl-icon": SlIcon, "sl-icon-button": SlIconButton, "sl-input": SlInput, "sl-popup": SlPopup, "sl-spinner": SlSpinner, "sl-tag": SlTag, "sl-tooltip": SlTooltip, }
members.description:
Shoelace components used inside the shadow root.

`LitElementWw` renders through a scoped custom element registry, so a tag
that is missing here stays an unknown element: the toolbar would show the
bare text of its buttons and options instead of the controls. The entries
also keep the component modules in the bundle, because the imports are
otherwise unused and get tree-shaken away. The list includes the elements
the components use in their own templates, because a scoped registry does
not inherit them from the global one.

members.name: pickerMode
members.description: Whether the rows act as an atom palette inside the Molecule Builder.

members.name: infoAnchor
members.description:
Free space the floating picker panel may occupy, in viewport coordinates.

The builder hands over the gap between its canvas cards, so the panel sits
in the canvas instead of beside the palette and never covers a card. The
rect is read on every reposition, which keeps the panel in place while the
page scrolls. Without an anchor the picker shows no panel.

members.name: #matching
members.description:
Atomic numbers the keyboard may reach.

In the grid this is every cell the mode can place, because the family filter
only fades a cell and leaves it clickable; in the list it is the rows that
survive the filter, because the list drops the rest.

members.name: #swapped
members.description:
Groups of card rows that show their alternate face.

The temperature unit stays across selections, because it is a preference
about the reading and not about one element; the structure face is reset
with the element, because the shell counts belong to its configuration.

members.name: #filtersOpen
members.description: Whether the panel with the search field and the family carousel is open.

members.name: #modesOpen
members.description: Whether the panel with the property modes and their slider is open.

members.name: #pickerInfo
members.description:
Element whose info panel floats beside the palette, `null` when closed.

The picker has no room for the inline card: the palette is a narrow column,
and the card would replace the row that is also the drag handle. The panel
therefore floats next to the entry it belongs to and leaves the list whole.

members.name: #dragOrigin
members.description:
Where the pointer pressed a drag handle, `null` outside a press.

The builder starts its drag after five pixels and does not suppress the
click that follows, so the picker compares the click with the press and
leaves the panel closed when the pointer travelled.

members.name: selectedAtomicNumber
members.description:
Currently selected atomic number, `null` when nothing is selected.

Live property without attribute reflection. Invalid writes are ignored and
keep the previous valid selection; a valid write dispatches no event.

members.name: effectiveView
members.description: Layout actually rendered: the learner's temporary choice wins over the author default.

members.name: clearInitialElement
members.description:
Removes the authored initial element.

The native number option cannot always be cleared in the editor, so authors
get an explicit action for it.

members.name: #observeLanguage
members.description: Watches every ancestor the language walk visits for a `lang` change.

members.name: #measure
members.description: Records the host width, which decides the automatic layout.

members.name: #captureResultFocus
members.description:
Remembers which result owns focus before the layout changes.

Only a focused result is restored; a click on a toolbar control leaves focus
where the user put it.

members.name: #reveal
members.description: Scrolls a focused result into the widget's own scroll area.

members.name: #language
members.description: Interface language of the surrounding content.

members.name: #resolvedView
members.description: Layout to render, with `auto` resolved against the measured width.

members.name: #temperature
members.description: Temperature the state rows and the cell colours refer to.

members.name: #placeable
members.description:
Atomic numbers of the cells the mode can place.

The grid renders these cells and fades the ones the family filter leaves
out, so this set is what the keyboard may reach there.

members.name: #matches
members.description:
Current search hits, best match first.

The query applies to both layouts: the search field sits in the filter
panel, which the ribbon opens in either view, so a query narrows the grid
and the list alike. The family filter is part of the same call, so the two
filters combine instead of replacing each other.

members.name: #selectFromUser
members.description:
Selects an element after a user action and reports the change.

A new element starts with the collapsed card: the open card covers the
cells below it, so it would hide the table the learner is browsing. The list
keeps its card open, but the row that was pressed is gone, so focus moves to
the card that replaced it.

members.name: #onRowClick
members.description:
Handles a click on a list row of the picker.

The symbol tile is the drag handle, so a click there only selects the
element; the rest of the row opens the info panel. The panel is the only
place the picker can show the element data, because the row itself has to
stay in place as the handle.

members.name: #draggedFromHandle
members.description:
Whether the click that follows a press on a drag handle belongs to a drag.

The builder starts its drag after five pixels and lets the click through,
so a drop would otherwise open the panel of the element that was just
placed. The press position is consumed here, because it describes one
gesture only.

members.name: #showPickerInfo
members.description: Opens the floating info panel of the picker, or closes it on a second click.

members.name: #closePickerInfo
members.description: Closes the floating info panel of the picker.

members.name: #onPickerKeydown
members.description:
Closes the floating panel on Escape.

The panel is not modal and keeps the focus on the row that opened it, so the
key is caught on the widget instead of on the card.

members.name: refreshInfoAnchor
members.description:
Re-reads the free space of the floating panel.

The panel is anchored to a live rect instead of an element, so the popup
cannot watch the boxes that bound it. The builder observes them and calls
this after they change: the render updates the height limit and the
reposition moves the panel.

members.name: #repositionPickerInfo
members.description:
Moves the floating panel onto the rect it is anchored to.

The popup only repositions itself when its own properties change, and the
anchor object stays the same while the gap around it moves. Every render
therefore asks for a fresh position, which reads the live rect again.

members.name: #listDetailsCard
members.description: The card that replaced the selected list row, if the list shows one.

members.name: #focusDetails
members.description: Focuses the card that replaced the selected list row.

members.name: #clearFromUser
members.description: Clears the selection after a user action and reports the change.

members.name: #toggleDetails

members.name: #toggleAlternate
members.description:

The value itself is the control and carries no mark, so the row reads as
plain text until it is used.

members.name: #onDetailsKeydown
members.description:
Closes the open detail card on Escape.

The card covers the cells below it, so the key that closes an overlay has to
work here as well. Focus stays on the toggle, which is still in the card.

members.name: #closeInfo

members.name: #onInfoHide

members.name: #focusElement

members.name: #reset

members.name: #resetMode
members.description:
Clears the property mode and restores the default thresholds.

The mode panel carries no `off` chip, so this is the way back to the plain
table. It also puts every slider back to the end that hides nothing, so the
next mode starts from the reference state instead of the last threshold.

members.name: #onQueryInput
members.description: Reads the search field.

members.name: #onSearchKeydown
members.description: Selects the best match on Enter, so the field works without a mouse.

members.name: #onCellKeydown
members.description:
Handles the grid keys of a cell.

Enter and Space activate the cell through the native click of the button
wrapper, so only the navigation keys are handled here. A handled key is
consumed, which keeps WebWriter's own shortcuts out of the grid; every other
key keeps its default and still reaches the editor.

members.name: #rovingTarget

parameters.name: matching
parameters.description: Atomic numbers that pass the current filter.

members.description: Picks the single cell that takes part in the tab order.

members.name: #renderCount
members.description: Renders the result count line.

members.name: #renderRibbon
members.description:
Renders the ribbon: the two layer toggles, the lip that carries both
layers, and the layout switch.

The ribbon is the only permanently visible band. The two toggles sit on the
left, the layout switch on the right, and between them one cutout anchors
the lip. The band itself is painted by a pseudo-element that keeps the
height of a single chip row, and the lip hangs below it as an absolutely
positioned layer, so the band never grows and the table below keeps its
box: an open layer covers the first rows of the table instead of pushing
them down. The lip carries the lifting shadow of the detail card, so it
reads as a layer above the table.

Both layers share the lip and stack inside it as two sections of their own,
so two open layers stay distinguishable without a divider between them. A
toggle shows a filled state while its layer is open and a small dot while
the layer is closed but still narrows the table, so a hidden filter never
looks like no filter at all.

members.name: #renderFilters
members.description:
Renders the filter layer inside the ribbon lip.

The panel holds the two controls that narrow the table, in the order they
are read: the search field with the reset beside it, then the family
carousel with the result count. Search and family filter combine, and both
apply to the grid and the list alike, because the panel is the same in both
layouts. The families are a Shoelace carousel of tags instead of a dropdown
plus a legend, because the tags double as the filter and the strip stays one
band at every width. It names itself through a hidden label instead of an
attribute, because the carousel writes its own generic label when it
connects. The reset sits outside the carousel, so it never scrolls out of
reach. The result count is a pill badge, and a hidden live region keeps the
full sentence for screen readers.

The panel is a section in the pattern of the chemicals drawer: a heading
band names the layer, the body holds the rows. That is what tells the two
layers of the lip apart without a divider between them.

members.name: #slider
members.description:
Describes the slider of the active mode.

Every mode reads its slider as a threshold and states the direction in the
readout, so the number alone cannot be misread: the radius keeps the elements
up to the value, the other three keep the ones from it upwards.

members.name: #renderModes
members.description:
Renders the property layer inside the ribbon lip.

The panel decides what the cells are coloured by: the state at the chosen
temperature, whether the element was already known in the chosen year, or
one of the four numeric properties. The modes sit in a carousel of chips, so
the row stays one band while the list of modes grows, and the slider of the
active mode sits underneath it with its value as a tag. The slider is a
native range input: it needs no component registration, keeps the keyboard
and touch behaviour of the platform, and cannot fall back to plain text when
a Shoelace build is missing. The legend of the temperature mode shares the
last row, because a row of its own would cost the table the height of one
period.

The strip carries no `off` chip. The reset beside it is the way back to the
plain table, in the same place and the same treatment as the reset beside
the search, so both panels clear their own state with one button at the end
of their row instead of a chip that scrolls away with the modes.

The panel is a section in the pattern of the chemicals drawer, like the
filter panel above it: a heading band names the layer, the body holds the
rows.

members.name: #renderStateLegend
members.description: Renders the colour key of the temperature mode.

members.name: #renderCell

parameters.name: roving
parameters.description: Atomic number of the tabbable cell.

parameters.name: faded
parameters.description: Whether the family filter leaves the cell out.

members.description:
Renders one element cell of the grid.

A cell the family filter does not match stays in place and fades instead of
disappearing: the table keeps its shape, so the learner still reads where
the family sits. Only a mode that cannot place an element removes its cell,
because a state or a year the model does not know would read as a value.

members.name: #renderGrid

parameters.name: matching
parameters.description: Atomic numbers that pass the current filter.

members.description:
Renders the table layout.

The detail card is a grid item of the table itself: it sits in the free block
above the transition metals, so the selection is read inside the table
instead of in a second column beside it. The card takes only the height of
its content, so the block keeps its own size and the periods around it never
stretch.

Every cell the mode can place is rendered; the family filter only fades the
cells it leaves out, so the table keeps its shape while the filter is on.
The series labels and the placeholder cards belong to the detached rows and
fade with them, because they name the same family.

members.name: #renderList

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: Selected element, or `null` when nothing is selected.

members.description:
Renders the list layout with the detail card in place of the selected row.

The card is always open here: the list has room for it, and a collapsed card
would only repeat the row it replaces. Rendering it instead of the row keeps
the identity of the element in one place, so the row and the card never show
the same name twice in two different styles. A selection the mode hides has
no row left, so its card moves to the top of the list.

members.name: #renderPrintOverview

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: Selected element, or `null` for the empty card.

members.description:
Renders the print-only overview.

The overview is always in the DOM and hidden on screen, so both author
layouts print the same complete grid and the selected details. It carries no
interactive element and is hidden from assistive technology, because the
screen layout already exposes the same content.

members.name: #renderDetails

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: Selected element, or `null` for the empty card.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Whether the card can collapse and whether it is open.

members.description:
Renders the detail card of one element.

The card is a Shoelace card, so it shares the surface and the border of the
rest of the widget. Its header carries the identity of the element in one
row. Below it the card shows the key rows — the weight and the answer of the
current mode — and stops there: the free block of the table is only three
rows tall, and a card that grew with its content would stretch the periods
around it. The toggle in the corner opens the rest as an overlay above the
cells. The list passes `collapsible: false`, because its card replaces the
selected row and has the room to stay open.

members.name: #renderPickerInfo
members.description:
Renders the floating info panel of the picker.

The panel describes an entry of the palette instead of replacing it,
because the entry has to stay in place as the drag handle. It carries the
same card as the standalone widget, minus the atom model view, and closes
through its own button or Escape. The builder hands over the gap between
its canvas cards, so the panel sits in the canvas and takes the height of
that gap; a short gap makes the body scroll instead of covering a card.

members.name: #renderDetailSections

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Rows the key rows do not already show.

members.description:
Renders the sections the expanded card adds.

A section without a row is dropped, which keeps the card free of empty
headings: the state row moves into the key rows in the temperature mode and
the discovery row in the discovery mode, so the section it came from can
become empty.

members.name: #renderDetailRow
members.description:
Renders one row of the detail card.

The state value is a tag in the colour of the state, so the value is legible
at a glance. A predicted value carries a badge instead of a bare word, and
the badge explains itself in a tooltip, so the card stays short without
hiding what the qualifier means. A row with an alternate face renders its
value as a button that swaps the two readings; the button is styled as the
text it replaces, because the card should not advertise a control it does
not need.

members.name: #renderInfo
members.description:
Renders the info dialog with the sources and the model notes.

The sources are global, not per element, so they sit behind one button in
the toolbar instead of in the detail card. Each source carries its release
as a badge and its licence and retrieval date as tags, which keeps the
block scannable while the attribution and the URL stay in running text.

events.description: After a user action that changed the selection.
events.name: chemlab:element-selection

attributes.name: initial-element
attributes.description: Authored default element, `null` for no initial selection.

attributes.name: view
attributes.description: Authored layout choice; invalid markup falls back to `auto`.

attributes.name: picker-mode
attributes.description: Whether the rows act as an atom palette inside the Molecule Builder.

members.name: #pickerAnchor
members.description:
Free space the picker info panel may occupy, in viewport coordinates.

The panel belongs to the periodic table, but the space it may use is the
gap between the two canvas cards, which only the builder can measure. The
rect is read on every reposition, so the panel follows the cards while
they grow and shrink.

members.name: #pickerGap
members.description:
Gap between the model summary and the selection card, in viewport pixels.

The picker info panel sits in the free strip of the canvas instead of
beside the palette, so it never covers the cards and never leaves the
widget. A short strip makes the panel scroll instead of growing over the
cards. Its left edge follows the selection card, which sits closest to
the palette, so the panel lines up with the bottom-left card and keeps
that edge when the selection appears.

members.name: #cardBox
members.description:
Box of a canvas card, or nothing when the card is hidden.

The model summary and the selection card stay in the template and are
hidden with an attribute, so a missing box has to count as an absent card
rather than as a card at the origin.

members.name: #observePickerGap
members.description:
Watches the boxes that bound the picker info panel.

The panel is anchored to a live rect, so nothing tells the popup when a
card grows. The observer asks the table to re-read the rect, which moves
the panel and updates its height limit. The cards come and go with the
structure, so the observed set is rebuilt after every render.

members.name: #centre
members.description: The view centre, so an atom can be placed without a pointer.

members.name: #hoverAtom
members.description:
Outline the atom a site chip belongs to, or clear the outline with
`undefined`. The 3D scene draws the ring itself, the 2D diagram reads the
same state, so both views answer a hover the same way.

members.name: #overPanel
members.description:
True when the event started inside a card that sits on the canvas and
scrolls on its own. Those cards keep their wheel and drag gestures, so a
scroll inside the selection card never turns into a zoom of the scene.

members.name: viewAtom
members.description: Opens an isolated element from another widget on the worksheet.

members.name: #renderCatalog
members.description:
The catalog opens as a flat list grouped by chemical class. A native select
would open a second dropdown on top of the popup, so every substance is a
row of its own. Its variants live in the model summary after selection.

members.name: #iconButton
members.description:
Renders a compact icon control, the shape the canvas controls share with
the lab. The label only lives in the tooltip and the accessible name, so
every caller has to pass one.

members.name: #renderSelectionCard
members.description: The selection card follows the lab's object info card and stays at the canvas edge.
